clue.text: Exhausted, Jeff loses his head on wrong tee

indicators.note: losing a head means the name drops its opening letter

parts.note: the name taken as written, before it is beheaded

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of their proper order and must be rearranged

parts.note: the golf peg taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer called Jeff, worn out, has lost his temper on the wrong tee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loses his head' sounds like a golfer's temper going, but it is the instruction to drop a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete describes someone feeble and worn out, having lost vigour; an older sense is literally exhausted or spent.

clue.text: New Year early bird: that's the top and bottom of it

parts.note: the top of a list or ranking is first place
the foot of a page or bed is its bottom

explanation.surface: Someone sums up an early New Year visitor with the phrase 'that's the top and bottom of it'.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland the first-foot is the first person over the threshold after midnight on New Year's Eve, traditionally bringing luck.
explanation.definitionFit: The first-foot arrives at the very start of the year, so they are literally its earliest visitor, a Scottish Hogmanay custom.

clue.text: Like horses featuring in the quinella

indicators.note: something featuring in a phrase is contained within its letters, so look inside the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the and most of quinella

explanation.surface: A racing tip: the horses that feature in a quinella bet, which picks the first two finishers.
explanation.walkthrough: A quinella is a bet on the first two finishers in either order, so the racing surface keeps the horse theme while hiding the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Equine is the adjective from Latin equus for anything relating to or resembling horses.

clue.text: Jeepers creepers! It's for bathing peepers!

definitions.text: Jeepers creepers! It's for bathing peepers!

parts.note: surface: an exclamation of surprise, the opening of the old song asking where you got those peepers
setter's reading: peepers is slang for eyes, so this is something you wash them with

explanation.surface: A burst of the song 'Jeepers Creepers', which asks where someone got those peepers.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyming exclamation is just colour taken from the song; the work is done by 'peepers', slang for eyes, and 'bathing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye lotion is a medicated liquid for washing or soothing sore eyes, which is exactly bathing the peepers.

clue.text: Make old seem new by making her revert to powder

indicators.note: to revert is to go back, so the pronoun is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
ash is the fine powder left after burning

explanation.surface: A cosmetic trick: rejuvenating a woman by having her go back to using face powder.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehash is to present old material again with only superficial changes, passing it off as fresh.

clue.text: Where cowboys show their skill, having sat on a duck

parts.note: to ride a horse is to sit on it, past tense here
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A cowboy showing off by riding a duck instead of a bronco.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman out for no runs scores a duck, so a duck is zero, the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a public contest where cowboys display roping and bronco-riding abilities.

clue.text: Preparatory study showing how to hold me — or the king

indicators.note: one word is made to hold the next, so it wraps around it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A lesson in wrestling holds: how to grip me, or how to grip the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Homework is the preparation done before a meeting or lesson, as well as schoolwork set to do at home.

clue.text: To be economical, finding money in the street

indicators.note: something found in a place sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: Thrift rewarded: a careful saver picks up money lying in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: Tin as slang for cash is old-fashioned British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To stint is to be sparing or frugal, giving or using only a meagre amount.

clue.text: Look at her suit, rumpled and bristly

indicators.note: a rumpled garment is crumpled out of shape, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone points out a woman's suit, creased and scratchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rumpled and bristly' seem to describe the suit's fabric; only 'bristly' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hirsute means hairy, and bristly describes something covered in short stiff hairs.

clue.text: Boisterousness means getting drunk on rum and vodka, say

parts.note: high is slang for intoxicated
rum and vodka are examples of distilled spirits, signalled by say

explanation.surface: A moralising remark that rowdiness comes from getting drunk on rum and vodka.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like one sentence of cause and effect, but it is HIGH 'on' SPIRITS in order.
explanation.definitionFit: High spirits are a lively, exuberant mood, the cheerful energy that shows itself as boisterousness.

clue.text: A politician ensnared by good-looker is a bit wet

indicators.note: something ensnared is caught inside a trap, so these pieces sit within another word

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
taken as written
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP charmed by an attractive admirer is called a bit of a wimp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit wet' looks like the British insult for feeble, but here it is literal moisture.
explanation.definitionFit: Dampish means slightly damp, and slightly damp is exactly being a little wet.

clue.text: Ceremonial soldiers had grousers all upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Parade-ground troops whose complainers have got everyone in a state.
explanation.walkthrough: The Horse Guards are the mounted Household Cavalry seen at ceremonies in London's Whitehall.
explanation.definitionFit: The Horse Guards are a British cavalry regiment best known for mounted duties at state ceremonies and parades.

clue.text: Find trouble in the bathroom

parts.note: the idiom for landing yourself in difficulties
setter's reading: literally climbing into a hot bath

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works twice: idiomatically it means landing in a scrape, literally it is what you do stepping into a hot bath.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to land oneself in difficulty or disgrace, while its literal sense is stepping into a hot bath.

clue.text: Catch sight of a pimple

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to notice or see
second meaning: a blemish on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone notices a blemish in the mirror.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to notice something; as a noun it is a small skin blemish or zit.

clue.text: Were gin twice shaken and stirred, you'd find alcohol in it

indicators.note: shaking and stirring mixes things up, so these letters are thoroughly rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the word gin written two times over

explanation.surface: A cocktail of double gin, shaken and stirred in Bond style, would certainly be alcoholic.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a loose description: this drink is one that contains alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger wine is a fortified drink made from fermented ginger and raisins, so it contains alcohol.

clue.text: Boatman makes do with one girl

indicators.note: makes suggests building something new out of the material, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boatman who gets by with just one girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes do' reads as one phrase meaning manages; split it, and makes is the signal while do is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondolier is the oarsman who propels and steers a Venetian gondola.

clue.text: Queen gets into smooth stockings in old railway engine

parts.note: to iron is to smooth out creases

indicators.note: getting into clothing means being inside it, so this letter goes within the garment word

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings
R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A queen pulling on her silky stockings aboard a vintage steam train.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron horse is an old-fashioned nickname for a steam locomotive, coined when trains replaced horses.

clue.text: "Goodbye" from a taxi passenger in fine fettle

parts.note: a cab driver's passenger is called a fare
in good health

explanation.surface: A cheerful cab passenger calls out a parting word as they get out.
explanation.definitionFit: Farewell is a word of parting, used just as one says goodbye when leaving.

clue.text: Physically fit, but falling behind in time

indicators.note: behind places the word before it after the pieces that follow, so it goes last

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: An athlete who is fit but nonetheless lagging behind on the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falling behind' looks like one phrase meaning lagging; split it, and behind places the falling word after IN T.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in training is following a fitness regime, keeping themselves in good physical condition.

clue.text: Soya bean curd is absorbed by the worst of us

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken right inside, so look within the following words

parts.note: spans the end of worst, all of of and the start of us

explanation.surface: A dig at vegetarian food: only the worst of us would soak up bean curd.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu is the pressed curd made by coagulating soya milk, a staple protein in East Asian cooking.

clue.text: Teetotaller in need is cleared

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

parts.note: taken as written
TT is the standard abbreviation for teetotal

explanation.surface: A sober person who has fallen into poverty has their debts written off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleared' looks like being let off, but in its money sense it means made as net profit.
explanation.definitionFit: To net or clear a sum is to make it as profit after all deductions, so netted is cleared.

clue.text: It's tricky lathering the toe when naked

indicators.note: something tricky is awkward and twisty, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bather admits that soaping your toes is awkward when you have no clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: The altogether is a humorous idiom for complete nudity, so someone in it is unclothed.

clue.text: Foot the bill for nurse

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to pay for someone else
second meaning: to give medical care to a patient

explanation.surface: Someone offers to pay a nurse's bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is just a joining word; it makes the surface read as paying on a nurse's behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat someone is both to pay their share and to give a patient medical care.

clue.text: A number left hanging up by a Russian revolutionary

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: nine is a number
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A hanging attributed to a Russian revolutionary, with a count of victims left on the gallows.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenin led the Bolsheviks in the 1917 Russian Revolution and founded the Soviet state.

clue.text: The lady has been in an illicit liquor-shop

parts.note: the pronoun for a lady
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gossip that a respectable woman has been seen in an unlicensed drinking den.
explanation.walkthrough: A shebeen is an Irish and Scottish word for an unlicensed bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an unlicensed drinking house selling alcohol without a permit, originally in Ireland.

clue.text: Incarcerates available sea birds

parts.note: someone in is at home and available
terns are slender seabirds

explanation.surface: Seabirds on offer are locked up, like caged stock.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern is to confine someone, especially in wartime, without trial, so it means imprisons.

clue.text: Filched a woman's shoulder garment at noon

parts.note: a stole is a wrap worn over the shoulders
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A woman's wrap was swiped at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: Stole as a garment hides alongside stole as the past tense of steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolen means taken without permission, and filched is a colloquial word for pilfered.

clue.text: More embarrassed, whichever way you look at it

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: reading from either end gives the same word, so it must be identical in both directions

parts.note: a more embarrassed face is one with a deeper blush

explanation.surface: Someone is even more mortified however the situation is viewed.
explanation.definitionFit: Embarrassment makes the face flush, so someone more embarrassed has a deeper blush in the cheeks.
